{{Missing information|the mathematics. So someone asked a question and someone else answered it. What is the question and what is the answer?|date=October 2022}}

The stability problem of [[functional equation]]s originated from a question of [[Stanisław Ulam]], posed in 1940, concerning the stability of [[group homomorphism]]s. In the next year, Donald H. Hyers<ref>D. H. Hyers, [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC1078310/pdf/pnas01627-0030.pdf ''On the stability of the linear functional Equation''], Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA, '''27'''(1941), 222-224.</ref> gave a partial affirmative answer to the question of Ulam in the context of [[Banach space]]s in the case of ''additive'' mappings, that was the first significant breakthrough and a step toward more solutions in this area. Since then, a large number of papers have been published in connection with various generalizations of Ulam's problem and Hyers's theorem. In 1978, [[Themistocles M. Rassias]]<ref>Th. M. Rassias, [https://www.jstor.org/stable/2042795?seq=1 ''On the stability of the linear mapping in Banach spaces''], Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. '''72'''(1978), 297–300.</ref> succeeded in extending Hyers's theorem for mappings between Banach spaces by considering an unbounded Cauchy difference<ref>D. H. Hyers, G. Isac and Th. M. Rassias, [http://www.zentralblatt-math.org/zmath/en/advanced/?q=an:0907.39025&format=complete ''Stability of Functional Equations in Several Variables''], [[Birkhäuser Verlag]], Boston, Basel, Berlin, 1998.</ref> subject to a continuity condition upon the mapping. He was the first to prove the stability of the ''linear mapping''. This result of Rassias attracted several mathematicians worldwide who began to be stimulated to investigate the stability problems of functional equations.

By regarding a large influence of [[Stanislaw Ulam|S. M. Ulam]], D. H. Hyers, and [[Th. M. Rassias]] on the study of stability problems of functional equations, the stability phenomenon proved by Th. M. Rassias led to the development of what is now known as Hyers–Ulam–Rassias stability<ref>''Hyers-Ulam-Rassias stability'', in: [[Encyclopaedia of Mathematics]], Supplement III, [[Michiel Hazewinkel|M. Hazewinkel]] (ed.), Kluwer Academic Publishers,  Dordrecht, 2001, pp.194-196.</ref> of [[functional equation]]s. For an extensive presentation of the stability of functional equations in the context of Ulam's problem, the interested reader is referred to the books by S.-M. Jung,<ref>S.-M. Jung, ''Hyers-Ulam-Rassias Stability of Functional Equations in Nonlinear Analysis'', Springer, New York (2011) {{isbn|978-1-4419-9636-7}}.</ref> S. Czerwik,<ref>S.Czerwik, ''Functional Equations and Inequalities in Several Variables'', World Scientific Publishing Co, Singapore (2002).</ref> Y.J. Cho, C. Park, Th.M. Rassias and R. Saadati,<ref>Y.J. Cho, C. Park, Th.M. Rassias and R. Saadati, ''Stability of Functional Equations in Banach algebras'', Springer, New York (2015).</ref> Y.J. Cho, Th.M. Rassias and R. Saadati,<ref>Y.J. Cho, Th.M. Rassias and R. Saadati, ''Stability of Functional Equations in Random Normed Spaces'', Springer, New York (2013).</ref> and Pl. Kannappan,<ref>Pl. Kannappan, ''Functional Equations and Inequalities with Applications'', Springer, New York (2009).</ref> as well as to the following papers.<ref>S.-M. Jung, ''Hyers-Ulam-Rassias stability of Jensen's equation and its application'', Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 126(1998), 3137-3143.</ref><ref>S.-M. Jung, ''On the Hyers-Ulam-Rassias stability of a quadratic functional equation'', J. Math. Anal. Appl. 232(1999), 384-393.</ref><ref>G.-H. Kim, ''A generalization of Hyers-Ulam-Rassias stability of the G-functional equation'', Math. Inequal. Appl. 10(2007), 351-358.</ref><ref>Y.-H. Lee and K.-W. Jun, ''A generalization of the Hyers-Ulam-Rassias stability of the pexider equation'', J. Math. Anal. Appl. 246(2000), 627-638.</ref> In 1950, T. Aoki<ref>T. Aoki, [http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?service=UI&version=1.0&verb=Display&handle=euclid.jmsj/1261735234 ''On the stability of the linear transformation in Banach spaces''], J. Math. Soc. Jpn., '''2'''(1950), 64-66.</ref> considered an unbounded Cauchy difference which was generalised later by Rassias to the linear case. This result is known as Hyers–Ulam–Aoki stability of the additive mapping.<ref>L. Maligranda, A result of Tosio Aoki about a generalization of Hyers-Ulam stability of additive functions–a question of priority, [[Aequationes Mathematicae]] 75 (2008), 289-296.</ref> Aoki (1950) had not considered continuity upon the mapping, whereas Rassias (1978) imposed extra continuity hypothesis which yielded a formally stronger conclusion.
